title: Edge-index publish tears down the prior complete view, so any rebuild failure or slow rebuild is a fenced outage for graph tools
wanted_capability: A selector-changing publish should carry the prior complete EdgeIndex into the new code read view and mark it stale rather than installing an empty index and lowering the readiness fence. Read-only graph consumers (bbox_inspect_entity, bbox_bundle_evidence, transcript hops) should be able to serve the stale-but-complete prior view with an explicit staleness marker while the watcher rebuilds, and a failed rebuild should never widen the outage beyond the rebuild itself. Fail-closed remains appropriate for writers such as provenance export, but that choice belongs to the consumer, not the fence.
missing_primitive: readiness-fence semantics that distinguish "prior view still complete but stale" from "no view available"; a code read view that retains the prior Arc<EdgeIndex> across publish
fallback_used: Callers retry after the watcher tick. The immediate-retry and coalesced-nudge fixes dispatched from thread-f51d2132 shrink the window but keep the tear-down-first swap.
evidence: src/server/code_source.rs activation and republish sites install EdgeIndex::default() in the same swap that lowers the fence
src/server/routes.rs manifest coordinator raises the fence only after a successful publish; a failed rebuild returns Err and the watcher sleeps the full interval

notes: Sibling of gap-71db0a11 (deferral branch leaves the fence down). This one covers the admitted-rebuild branch: the fence is down for the whole rebuild plus any retry because the prior index was discarded at publish time.
